title: [TRACKER] Joypad issues
body:
current state of this issue tracker; will write a comment in this issue when these tasks are done:
* [x] going through all open issues
* [ ] re-order/re-categorize listed issues
* [x] look through proposals
* [ ] point out root issues identified in certain issues

---


joypad database
* Godot's state: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/core/input/gamecontrollerdb.txt
  * plus Godot's overwrite: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/core/input/godotcontrollerdb.txt
* source we copy from: https://github.com/mdqinc/SDL_GameControllerDB
* notes regarding GUID: they are unique per joypad, and even for the same joypad, it can be a different GUID depending on
  * firmware/driver version
  * API (some platforms have multiple APIs)


about drivers
* Linux
  * try `xpadneo-dkms-git` instead of `xone`, [as the latter seems to have issues](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/65308#issuecomment-2129447982)

in general
* about joypads: https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Gamepad

Testing your joypad:
* web: https://hardwaretester.com/gamepad
* android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=uk.co.powgames.gamecondiag
  * this is just a random example, which has not been tested or verified in any way
* Godot: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/misc/joypads
* testing different mapping: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/inputs/controllers_gamepads_joysticks.html#my-controller-has-incorrectly-mapped-buttons-or-axes
* create bindings yourself using https://generalarcade.com/gamepadtool/
* you can use `evtest`/`evemu-record` to test the keycode mapping of the controller on Linux


Legend for hardwaretester.com
* Axis
  * 9: is the "Hat Switch" axis which encodes the D-pad state as a clockwise rotational value from 0 (north) to 7 (northwest). When the D-pad is in its neutral state it sends an out-of-bounds value. This is expected for HID gamepads without a mapping function. [[source](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40747349)]

## Design/Root Issues

* connection issues
  * driver calls can hang main thread: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/105271#issuecomment-2797206325
  * bluetooth:
    * https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101382
    * https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102703
  * device is mapped twice
    * https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/76724 which is **not fixed**
    * https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/90795, which has a fixing PR
    * https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/50273, which has a fixing PR
* button binding database: heavy reliance on manual updates
  * [ ] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/38048
  * [x] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/78805
    * reproducible in Godot: 3.5.2, 4.0.3, 4.1 rc, 4.2.1, 4.3
    * **not** reproducible in Godot: 3.2.3
* device ID
  * [ ] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/105458
  * see also `Improved Multiplayer support`
* device names: see also https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/89193
  * [x] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/98008
  * [x] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/96756
* see `deadzone issues`  and `axis issues`, plus
  * https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3709#issuecomment-1164624685
    * `Also, it seems like the current system kind of leads to some sort of confusion. On the one hand, the deadzone is used as a way to filter out garbage events sent by your OS (for joysticks), but on the other hand it is used as a trigger value for boolean (pressed/not pressed) actions.`
* event processing
  * [ ] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/99513
    * reproducible in Godot: 4.2.2, 4.3, but probably all Godot versions
    * a `joy_hat` event, which are hardcoded to map to the dpad, generates 2 button events [[source](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/42200#issuecomment-2714414966)]. A press in one direction, clears the direction value into the other direction [[source](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/99513#issuecomment-2495419652)].
    * solution: The best option might be to _not_ automatically release the opposite button [[source](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/42200#issuecomment-2714575049)]
  * [ ] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/90516
    * reproducible in Godot: 4.2.1
  * [ ] https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/99331
    * assumed duplicate of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/90516
    * when using [shortcuts](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_shortcut.html), the button will not trigger it's pressed signal
    * note: `InputEventJoypadMotion is excluded from shortcut processing […]. I tried adding JoypadMotion to that list, similar to other event types. It did make it possible to trigger shortcuts with it, but the shortcuts fired every time the joypad motion event was received, not just once.` [[source](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/99331#issuecomment-2798519814)]
    * reproducible in Godot: 4.3
